segments.summary: A deck-level lift failure would hinder HMS Hermes but could be managed; a lift jammed below deck would be a much more serious operational problem.
segments.question: How would HMS Hermes cope if its centreline lift jammed at flight-deck level throughout the 1982 Falklands conflict?
segments.answerShort: A lift stuck level with the deck would be inconvenient but survivable; one jammed down would create a much more severe obstruction to aircraft operations.

segments.title: The Bank of England, public finance, and naval power
segments.body: The Bank of England was created to put government finances in order rather than solely to build the Royal Navy. A stronger fiscal system did assist the creation and support of the fleet, but that naval effect followed from the wider financial function. The distinction matters because an institution can strengthen sea power without existing solely as a naval organisation.

evidence.note: The Bank of England's government-finance purpose and the resulting assistance to naval development.

segments.summary: The Bank of England organised government finance, which in turn helped support greater naval capacity.
segments.question: Was the Bank of England created to build the Royal Navy?
segments.answerShort: No. It was created to organise government finances, which in turn helped the state create and support the Royal Navy.

segments.title: Mahan's influence on capital-ship treaty categories
segments.body: Selective attention to Mahan's emphasis on battleships and battle is offered as one reason for using a combined capital-ship category. A different treaty could have allocated Britain and the United States fifteen battleships and five battlecruisers each. Japan could have received nine battleships and three battlecruisers, forcing a decision about one of its four Kongos. France and Italy might have received seven battleships and two battlecruisers each after rounding the proposed ratios. Those hypothetical allocations would have changed what each navy retained or built, particularly French and Italian battlecruiser development.

evidence.note: Interpretation of Mahan's reception and hypothetical separate battleship and battlecruiser allocations.

segments.summary: Selective reading of Mahan is linked to a combined capital-ship category, with a hypothetical alternative showing the effect on fleet composition.
segments.question: Did Mahan's thinking guide American thinking about naval treaties?
segments.answerShort: In this interpretation, attention to selected parts of Mahan encouraged a combined capital-ship category instead of separate battleship and battlecruiser allocations.

segments.title: Treaty speed limits for different capital ships
segments.body: A hypothetical treaty could cap battleship design speed at 28 knots and require battlecruisers to exceed 30 or even 32 knots. Both categories could retain guns and armour within an equal 35,000-ton allowance. The speed requirements would constrain what designers could achieve inside that displacement. The later London treaty treatment of sloops, cited here as limited to a 20-knot design speed, supplies a comparison.

evidence.note: Hypothetical capital-ship speed definitions at 35,000 tons and the London treaty sloop comparison.

segments.summary: Different speed limits could keep battleships and battlecruisers distinct under an equal displacement allowance.
segments.question: How could a treaty keep battleships and battlecruisers from merging into one category?
segments.answerShort: Set a maximum design speed for battleships and a higher minimum for battlecruisers, while allowing the same displacement limit.

segments.title: A tentative estimate of Type 83 fleet size
segments.body: Six to eight Type 83 ships is a tentative estimate. Economic and strategic developments could change the number.

evidence.note: Tentative estimate of six to eight hulls and its economic and strategic qualifications.

segments.summary: The suggested six to eight Type 83 ships depends on future economic and strategic conditions.
segments.question: How many Type 83 ships might be built?
segments.answerShort: Possibly six to eight, depending on economic and strategic developments.
